A dented hollow plastic shark, its dorsal fin a faded yellow cutting the surface, runs a hard line of broken foam straight down the fleet's port side, one painted eye staring forward, a bite torn clean through the trailing edge of its tail.

A long low rubber crocodile, sun-faded from vivid green to the colour of old copper, rides the surface with only its ridged back and two orange painted eyes showing, moving astern of the fleet with the slow patience of something that has already decided.

A moulded plastic barracuda, its flanks a deep electric blue worn to bare pale plastic along the belly seam, holds perfect station three inches off the lead vessel's bow, facing into the current, motionless except for the tiny oscillation of the surface against its chin.

A hollow plastic whale, cobalt blue with a squeaker hole gaping at the top of its head, rolls up from below and lifts the nearest vessel on a slow swell of displaced water, one painted white eye breaking the surface first, the rest of it rising after.

A rubber hippo, its back a wide wet expanse of scuffed terracotta orange, sits half-submerged off the starboard quarter, the surface lapping at its nostrils, its four stubby legs planted on the enamel bottom below, watching the fleet pass with two small black painted eyes.

A hollow plastic turtle, its domed shell cracked along the left rear quarter and gone soft and pale at the crack, pulls itself forward at the edge of frame, half-awash, each stroke of its faded lime-green flippers raising a small white disturbance that closes behind it.

A scuffed rubber walrus, tusks a chipped cream-white, rolls to one side in the wake of the fleet with its pale belly breaking the surface, one flipper raised and braced, its mould seam running in a dark line from chin to tail.

A plastic narwhal, its spiral horn a faded candy-pink that was once vivid magenta, cuts the surface ahead and to port at a slight angle, the horn piercing the meniscus first, a fan of water spreading along it as the creature drives forward into open water.

A scuffed rubber octopus, its body deep violet and wedged into a clump of loofah fibres caught against the far side, extends one arm out across the open water toward the fleet, the arm's underside showing a row of moulded pale suckers, the rest of it still and waiting.

A plastic seahorse, its body a saturated tangerine orange with one painted eye sitting noticeably higher than the other, stands bolt upright in six inches of still water off the shallows, its curled tail anchored to a strand of loofah, drifting just enough to watch the fleet go by.

A jelly-mould jellyfish pressed from translucent soft plastic in a deep rose pink, drifts at the surface with the water moving visibly through its open underside, four moulded tentacles trailing behind it, the pink saturating deep where the plastic is thickest.

A rubber snake, vivid cadmium yellow with a repeating chevron pattern in chewed and flaking red, coils itself along the surface in three loose rings, the raised coils catching water that rolls off the sides, its blunt moulded head lifted a half-inch clear, facing the oncoming bow.

A squeaky plastic crab, fire-engine red with one claw larger than the other from a moulding error nobody corrected, works its way along the back of a grounded bar of soap at the waterline, each leg finding a grip in the eroded surface, moving sideways and intent.

A plastic starfish, flat and a hard saturated gold, presses itself against the wet enamel just above the waterline at the frame's edge, five arms spread, water beaded along each raised moulded ridge, its underside suckered flat to the white enamel.

A wind-up plastic fish, its key still engaged and spinning, thrashes across the surface in a hard zigzag of orange and teal, the wound spring driving its tail so fast the motion blurs, throwing small fans of white water to both sides as it crosses directly ahead of the fleet.

A hollow plastic pelican, white gone to a yellowed ivory with its great orange pouch chewed soft and slightly deflated, sits high on the water off the fleet's bow, the pouch swinging with each small wave, a hairline crack running from the base of its beak to one painted blue eye.

A dozen tiny moulded plastic fish, a dozen of them, each one a vivid tropical yellow, pack into a tight turning mass just beneath the surface, their shadows making one large moving shape on the bright enamel below, the ball folding and refolding as one organism.

A scatter of small moulded plastic minnows, translucent green with a stripe of silver paint worn thin along each flank, hangs just under the meniscus in a loose drift, each one angled slightly nose-up, their shadows distinct on the bright enamel below, still and bright as the fleet's wake reaches them.

Two rubber frogs, one a loud lime green and one a sun-faded teal with a bite torn from its left rear leg, sit back on their haunches on the curved back of a floating sponge, watching the fleet's passage with four black painted eyes, both of them dead still.

A plastic dolphin, its body a deep cerulean blue with a belly of faded white, arcs clear of the surface ahead of the fleet, the water running off it in separate fast-moving drops that trail behind the curve of its jump before the surface takes them back.

A rubber seal, charcoal grey on its back and a surprised pale cream on its belly, rolls at the surface with that belly turned skyward, one flipper breaking clear of the water, its painted black eye looking straight up, the mould seam running the full length of its underside.

A grey plastic manta, its wingspan wider than the fleet's broadest vessel, passes underneath the hulls low over the bright enamel, seen down through clear water as a flat pale cross moving slowly forward, the tips of its wings flexing in the current, its long thin tail trailing behind.

A moulded hollow plastic stingray, its topside a deep burnt sienna and its underside a pale bare plastic where the paint stops, glides forward just beneath the surface close astern, its wide flat body undulating in a slow wave from front edge to trailing tip as it closes the gap.

A rubber puffer fish, inflated to a hard round ball of faded tangerine with short blunt plastic spines pressed flat from years of handling, bobs in the fleet's wake, spinning slowly, its two painted black eyes on opposite sides of its head each catching the light at a different moment.

A moulded plastic eel, its body a deep electric purple with a chewed and ragged tail where the rubber has torn and been compressed back into a blunt end, moves in long lateral curves through the water alongside the fleet, each curve displacing the surface in a low rolling motion that reaches the nearest hull.
